AMALGAM
(Flavor needed)

See Amalgam Variant Features. Strands: Diablan Meter, Draconic Meter, Fey Meter, Giant Meter, Hive Meter, Leviathan Meter, Revenant Meter.
Strands (1)
Strands are investable gauges of different supernatural forces, invested into with Potency. Each time you level up, you may reassign up to half of your currently invested Potency, losing the benefits of the meters you’ve invested in.
Dominant Graft (2)
Select one Strand you are invested in. This is your Dominant Strand. It becomes the most visually apparent, and those who recognize the species that Strand hails from recognize you as someone possessing something from it.
You gain the following attack:























NameAttributeSkillDieTypeReachPropertiesUnleash StrandMight/SpeedHandled6Blunt1
Your Unleash Strand is further modified by your Dominant Strand. A Meter’s modifications to Unleash Strand only apply while that Strand is Dominant.
Adaptive (3)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When you take damage to your Vitality from a damage type other than Anomalous, you may gain -1 Defense against that type for the rest of the encounter, to a maximum of -3.
Foreign Kinship (4)
You can nonverbally communicate with entities of a species the Strand hails from. You gain 1d4 for every Potency you’ve invested in that Strand on Speak rolls against them, and you gain 1d6 for every Potency you’ve invested in that Strand on Resist rolls made to defend against effects they’d impose upon you.
Overgrowth (5)
Turn: Once per breather, you may treat one Strand as having 1 additional Potency invested, ignoring your Cap, until the end of the encounter.
Elastic Form (6)
Your Reach increases by 1.
Retoughened Skin (7)
The first time you use Adaptive after each of your turns, it costs no Momentum.
Splice (8)
When you Hone, you may move 1 invested Potency from one Strand to another until the end of the encounter.
Primal Weapon (9)
Your Unleash Strand’s die size increases by 1 step (to a maximum of d12), and it gains Reinforced 1. If it’s already a d12, it gains Reinforced 2 instead.
Hardened Adaptation (10)
Adaptive grants -2 Defense per use instead of -1, still limited by its maximum.
Living Armory (11)
When you attack with your Unleash Strand, you may change its damage type to Blunt, Slice, or Puncture.
Perfect Organism (12)
Turn: Once per rest, each Strand you have invested in counts as having 2 additional Potency invested, to a maximum of 5, until the end of the encounter.

rules/classes/amalgam/amalgam-variant-fe.title: Amalgam Variant Features
rules/classes/amalgam/amalgam-variant-fe.content:
AMALGAM VARIANT FEATURES
See Amalgam Core Class.
Strong Prey (1)
Your maximum Vitality increases by 3.
Swift Predator (1)
When you complete a Sprint, you may attempt a Grab.
Double Helix (2)
Your Unleash Strand attack gains Flurry.
Mental Reserves (2)
When your Periphery is broken, you instantly gain 3 Momentum.
Gluttonous (3)
You may consume anything, including foreign objects that are typically unsafe to eat.
When you successfully grab an entity, you may inflict 1 Chemical damage.
You gain /2 Chemical Defense against Chemical damage taken through consumption.
Marrow Reserves (3)
When you level up, you may opt to not fully invest all of your Potency.
At any time, you may invest your banked Potency to gain new corresponding features.
Shifting Dominance (4)
When you Hone, you may make a different invested Strand your Dominant Strand until the end of the encounter.
Regenerating Wounds (4)
Each rest restores 3 Vitality, and your maximum Vitality increases by 4.
Melt Away (5)
Turn: You (and any of your equipment that you choose) transform into a viscous fluid for 10 Counts, losing all Momentum, gaining /2 Defense against all damage (except Anomalous), becoming Unconscious, and seeping through cracks. When you reform into your original form, you awaken, and reappear in whichever unoccupied space you can fit in that is closest to the majority of the liquid.
Shed Skin (5)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When you are Grabbed, you may end the grab, leaving your grabber holding a husk.
Enhanced Adaptation (6)
Adaptive may gain Defense up to -6.
Predatory Sense (6)
You perceive every living entity within 3 spaces of you, even without sight.
Venom Glands (7)
Your Unleash Strand deals 1 extra Chemical damage when it damages a target’s Vitality.
Vestigial Limb (7)
You gain one additional hand.
Apex Appetite (8)
Prerequisite: Gluttonous
When you consume a creature’s flesh during a breather, one Strand that creature’s species hails from counts as having 1 additional Potency invested until your next rest.
Siphon Graft (8)
When your Unleash Strand reduces a hostile entity to 0 Vitality, you gain 2 Momentum.
Chrysalis (9)
Prerequisite: Melt Away
You choose how many Counts your Melt Away lasts, up to 10. Once per rest, when you reform, you restore 2 Vitality.
Unbound Adaptation (9)
Prerequisite: Enhanced Adaptation
Adaptive no longer possesses a numerical limit it can progress to within an encounter.
Chimeric Lungs (10)
You can breathe in any fluid or gas, and you gain (Speed) Swim.
Fluid Dominance (10)
Prerequisite: Shifting Dominance
You may change your Dominant Strand at the start of any of your turns, not only when you Hone.
Pack Scent (11)
Allies within 3 spaces of you add your Foreign Kinship dice to their Speak rolls.
Unkillable (11)
Prerequisite: Melt Away
Once per rest, when you would be reduced to 0 Vitality, you may use Melt Away instead, without spending a turn.
Apex Predator (12)
When your Unleash Strand hits, you may spend 2 Momentum to make another Unleash Strand attack against the same target.
Endless Evolution (12)
Prerequisite: Unbound Adaptation
Adaptive’s Defense lasts until your next rest instead of the end of the encounter.

rules/classes/amalgam/diablan-meter.title: Diablan Meter
rules/classes/amalgam/diablan-meter.content:
DIABLAN METER
An Amalgam Strand. It hails from a species fused from devils and demons.
1 - Hateful Skin
Unleash Strand grants you 1 Periphery when it damages a target’s Vitality.
You gain -1 Defense against Necrotic, and can perceive up to 6 spaces in any direction in lightless environments.
2 - Boiling Blood
When you take damage to your Vitality, all enemies within 1 space of you (orthogonally or diagonally) take 1 Heat.
3 - Pactmaker
You may make a deal with a fellow entity of 2 or higher Mind. Upon shaking hands, both of you are instantly compelled to uphold your ends of the deal made, and are considered hypnotized until their end is met.
4 - Smell Desires
You gain the ability to instantly know the number one desire of any person after at least a minute of communication.
You may burn an item to dust, and you become aware of the location of the individual who is the majority owner of that item.
5 - Shadow Seams
At the end of a round, you may make an attack from a space below you. You must Hone before being able to do this again.

rules/classes/amalgam/draconic-meter.title: Draconic Meter
rules/classes/amalgam/draconic-meter.content:
DRACONIC METER
An Amalgam Strand. It hails from dragons.
1 - Serpentine
Unleash Strand’s attack total is increased by 1.
Turn: An enemy must make a Grit-Resist roll against your Charm-Instinct roll, or gain 1 stack of Frightened of you.
2 - Kindled
You gain -1 Defense against Heat.
Turn: You ignite something by breathing gently upon it. It catches fire. If it’s alive, it becomes Burning.
3 - Scaled
You gain -1 Defense against Blunt, Slice, and Puncture.
4 - Unyielding
You gain 2 flat successes on rolls defending against Chronal spells. Additionally, you no longer age.
5 - Hoarding
You gain 1 flat success on Find rolls, you gain /2 Defense against Heat, and you gain (Speed+1) Flight.

rules/classes/amalgam/fey-meter.title: Fey Meter
rules/classes/amalgam/fey-meter.content:
FEY METER
An Amalgam Strand. It hails from the fey.
1 - Flicker
Unleash Strand’s attack total is increased by 1. When it hits, you may teleport 1 space.
2 - Glamoured
While your Periphery isn’t broken, your Evasion is increased by 1.
You gain -1 Defense against Psychic.
3 - Point of View
Once per round, when an ally within 3 spaces is attacked, you may swap places with them, and the attack targets you instead.
Unleash Strand deals 1d4 extra damage.
4 - Persona
Your Sidestep grants 1 additional Evasion.
Turn: You take the appearance and size of an entity of your size or smaller that you have seen, until your next rest.
5 - Blinking Onslaught
Flicker may teleport you up to your Move.
Point of View’s 1d4 becomes 1d6.

rules/classes/amalgam/giant-meter.title: Giant Meter
rules/classes/amalgam/giant-meter.content:
GIANT METER
An Amalgam Strand. It hails from giants.
1 - Vast
Your size increases in dimension by 1 space.
Unleash Strand adds 1d4 to its weapon die.
2 - Fleshscape
You gain -2 Defense against Cold and Heat. You gain 2 flat successes on rolls made to resist the temperatures of environments, any source of Cold damage, and any source of Heat damage.
3 - Earthshaker
When your Unleash Strand damages the Vitality of a target smaller than you, it becomes Fallen Over.
4 - Old Blood
Your Might is considered 2 higher for lifting, carrying, and resisting being moved.
5 - Colossus
Your size increases in dimension by 1 additional space. Entities smaller than you cannot Grab or move you.

rules/classes/amalgam/hive-meter.title: Hive Meter
rules/classes/amalgam/hive-meter.content:
HIVE METER
An Amalgam Strand. It hails from swarming insects.
1 - Marked Prey
When Unleash Strand hits, the target becomes Marked until the end of the encounter. Only one entity may be Marked at a time. You and your allies gain +1 to attack totals against it.
2 - Compound Eyes
You gain -1 Defense against Chemical.
You see in every direction, and you gain 1 flat success on sight-based Find rolls.
3 - Shared Senses
You and allies within 6 spaces perceive anything any of you perceive.
You and your allies deal 1d4 extra damage to your Marked entity.
4 - Disperse
Interruption (2 Momentum): When an attack hits you, halve its damage and move 2 spaces, passing through entities.
5 - Stinging Cloud
When you take damage to your Vitality, every entity within 1 space gains 1 stack of Staggered.
Marked Prey’s bonus becomes +2.

rules/classes/amalgam/leviathan-meter.title: Leviathan Meter
rules/classes/amalgam/leviathan-meter.content:
LEVIATHAN METER
An Amalgam Strand. It hails from ancient aquatic forces.
1 - Undertow
Unleash Strand deals 1d4 extra damage, which becomes 1d8 against an entity you have Grabbed. When it hits, you may pull the target 1 space toward you.
You can breathe underwater.
2 - Drag Under
Interruption (2 Momentum): When Unleash Strand hits, you may attempt a Grab against the target.
You gain (Speed) Swim.
3 - Constrictor
At the end of each of your turns, entities you have Grabbed take Blunt damage equal to your Potency invested in this Strand.
Undertow’s 1d4 becomes 1d6.
4 - Crushing Depth
Entities you have Grabbed cannot spend Momentum.
Undertow’s 1d6 becomes 1d8.
5 - Maw
You may have 2 entities Grabbed at once.

rules/classes/amalgam/revenant-meter.title: Revenant Meter
rules/classes/amalgam/revenant-meter.content:
REVENANT METER
An Amalgam Strand. It hails from the undead.
1 - Grave Hunger
Unleash Strand deals 1d4 extra Necrotic damage. When it damages a target’s Vitality, you regain 1 Vitality.
You do not need to breathe.
2 - Cold Flesh
You gain -1 Defense against Cold and Necrotic.
3 - Death’s Door
While at half your Vitality or lower, you gain -2 Blunt / Puncture / Slice Defense.
Grave Hunger’s 1d4 becomes 1d6.
4 - Grave Whisper
Turn: Ask a corpse one question, which it answers with what it knew in life. Each corpse may only be asked once.
5 - Return to Rest
Once per rest, when you would be reduced to 0 Vitality, you instead become Unconscious until the end of the round or until damaged, with Vitality equal to your Grit.

rules/classes/jester/jester-core-class.title: Jester Core Class
rules/classes/jester/jester-core-class.content:
JESTER

See Jester Variant Features.
Audience (1)
You have a number of Spectators at any given time, which dictates your capacity to entertain and accomplish tasks.
If an entity is sentient enough to recognize you, is visually (or audibly, if you are verbally making sounds) perceiving you, you are visually or audibly perceiving them, and they are explicitly not an ally, they count as 1 Spectator.
You possess an Audience Die, which is a single die with a size equal to the number of Spectators rounded down to the biggest available size (or a d4 if there is no die size to round down to), to a maximum of a d12.





























SpectatorsAudience Die0-5d46-7d68-9d810-11d1012+d12
Once per roll, you may add your Audience Die to a test roll that does not use Mind or Grit. Like any die, it may explode on a maximum roll.
You may use your Audience Die in place of your Skill die on an attack roll that does not use Mind or Grit.
Worn Mask (2)
Choose your Mask from the following options, gaining features from this choice immediately and your Worn Features.

Mask of the Fool

Enthralling (3)
Turn: Make a Charm-Speak roll against all Spectators. Spectators with a Mind lower than your successes gain 1 stack of Staggered.
Encore (4)
When an entity would stop counting as a Spectator because it fell over, became Unconscious, left your perception, or became your ally, it continues to count toward your Audience Die’s size until the end of the encounter.
Stage Presence (6)
Once per breather, you may add your Audience Die to a roll, regardless of prior limitations.
Grand Gesture (7)
Turn: Choose Mockery, Menace, or Mayhem. Make a Charm-Speak roll. Every Spectator must contest with a Mind-Resist roll, and every one who fails suffers the chosen effect:

Mockery: They become Hypnotized (Transfixed) by you until you take damage.
Menace: They gain 1 stack of Frightened of you.
Mayhem: They gain 2 stacks of Staggered.

Troupe Leader (9)
Interruption (1 Momentum): You may add your Audience Die to an ally’s roll.
Palmed Card (10)
When you Hone, draw a card. This is your Palmed Card, and it is kept between rounds (you may keep it face down to keep track of it being your Palmed Card). You may only have one Palmed Card at a time. It is added to your hand, and you may play it on its respective Count to take a turn instantly. During the turn in which you play your Palmed Card, your Audience Die has its explosion range increased by 1.
The Show Must Go On (12)
Once per rest, when you would be reduced to 0 Vitality, roll (Charm)d(Audience Die), and instead be reduced to Vitality equal to your successes.

rules/classes/jester/jester-variant-feat.title: Jester Variant Features
rules/classes/jester/jester-variant-feat.content:
JESTER VARIANT FEATURES
See Jester Core Class.
True Performer (1)
On an attack roll, you may use your Audience Die in place of your Skill die, your weapon die, or your Attribute.
Upstage (1)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When an ally within your melee reach is attacked, you may make an opposed Charm-Speak roll against the attacker’s Mind-Instinct roll. If you win, you are attacked instead.
You gain 1 Spectator for the encounter, to a maximum of 2 Spectators gained this way.
Cap and Bells (2)
If your Audience Die is a d6 or larger, you gain 1 Momentum at the end of your first turn each round. If it is unspent by the start of your second turn, you lose it.
Cheap Shot (2)
You deal 1 extra damage to entities not counting toward your Spectators.
Juggler (3)
When your hands are all filled by different one-handed objects, you may hold 1 additional object that is considered to be held by any 1 of your hands at a time.
Pratfall (3)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When you are grabbed while standing, you may make an attack against the grabber. You take half the damage this deals, and both you and the grabber become Fallen Over.
Comical Protection (4)
Once per round, you may Sidestep a Spectator’s attack without spending Momentum.
Killing Joke (4)
When you reduce a Spectator to 0 Vitality, every other Spectator must make a Charm-Resist roll against your Charm-Speak. Those who fail gain 1 stack of Frightened of you.
Captive Audience (5)
Spectators that you know to be Staggered, Frightened, or Hypnotized count as 2 toward your Audience Die’s size.
Crowd Surfer (5)
You may move through spaces occupied by enemies. The first time each turn that you leave the reach of a hostile Spectator, you may make a Charm-Speak roll against their Mind-Instinct. On a win, they gain 1 stack of Staggered.
Capacity Crowd (6)
Your minimum Audience Die size is a d6, and your features all treat you as having at least 6 Spectators, regardless of the conditions.
Standing Ovation (6)
When a hostile Spectator’s Periphery is broken by an ally, one of you gains 2 Momentum, and the other gains 4 Periphery.
Heel Turn (7)
You gain the Retaliate tactic. When you use Retaliate against a Spectator, you may add your Audience Die to its attack roll (which does not count as your per-roll Audience Die use).
Upgraded Upstage (7)
Prerequisite: Upstage
Your Upstage may target any allies you can perceive where you are also targetable by the attacker.
Débatteur (8)
Entities contesting your Charm-Speak have their success threshold increased by 1.
Unforgettable (8)
Prerequisite: Encore
Your Spectator count includes every unique Spectator you have acquired throughout this scene, even after they fall, leave, or no longer perceive you.
Lucky Day (9)
Your Audience Die has its explosion range increased by 1. If it explodes, the Audience Die added has its explosion range increased by 1 more. This repeats with each successive exploded Audience Die.
Sleight of Hand (9)
Interruption (2 Momentum): When a Spectator would begin their turn on a Count you share a card with, make an opposed Speed-Handle roll against their Mind-Instinct. If you win, they must skip their turn entirely. An entity becomes immune to Sleight of Hand for the remainder of the scene after being targeted with it, success or fail.
Apathy Act (10)
Interruption (3 Momentum): When you are reduced to 0 Vitality, you may take a turn before the reduction resolves, but after the blow is dealt.
Sympathy Act (10)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When your Periphery is broken, you may make a Charm-Speak roll against the attacker who broke it, who must make a Grit-Instinct roll. If they fail, they become Hypnotized (Charmed) for 6 Counts.
Curtain Caller (11)
When you deal Vitality damage to a Spectator, they gain 1 stack of Fatigue.
Enforced Clownery (11)
When an ally uses your Audience Die on an opposed roll, they may double the number of successes granted by your Audience Die.
Consummate Performer (12)
When you add your Audience Die, you may add a second Audience Die that is 1 die size smaller than your first. When you use your Audience Die on an attack roll, it is 1 die size larger.
One-Person Show (12)
Prerequisite: Capacity Crowd
Your minimum Audience Die size is a d10, and your features all treat you as having at least 10 Spectators, regardless of the conditions.

rules/classes/jester/mask-of-the-fool.title: Mask of the Fool
rules/classes/jester/mask-of-the-fool.content:
MASK OF THE FOOL
A Jester Mask.
Worn Features
Heckle (2)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When a Spectator hits with an attack, roll your Audience Die and reduce the attack’s damage by its total.
Tomfoolery (5)
When a Spectator’s roll is reduced to 0 successes, or their attack’s damage is reduced to 0, by your Heckle, gain 1 Spectator for the encounter (to a maximum gained this way equal to your Charm).
Egg on Your Face (8)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When a Spectator misses an attack against you, they gain 1 stack of Staggered. If they are already Staggered, you may make an attack against them instead.
Lord of Misrule (11)
Your Heckle can affect any roll a Spectator makes, not just their attack rolls. On a test roll, it removes successes equal to your Audience Die’s successes. Whenever a Spectator’s roll is reduced to 0 successes by this, you regain the 1 Momentum spent on it.

rules/classes/lorewalker/lorewalker-core.title: Lorewalker Core Class
rules/classes/lorewalker/lorewalker-core.content:
LOREWALKER
(Flavor needed)

See Lorewalker Variant Features and Lorewalker Heirlooms.
Tablet of Lore (1)
You possess a Tablet of Lore, which is a recordkeeping means of your choice (usually a thin, carved-into plate of stone). This manifests to you as a grid of a certain size, as shown in the Grid Size column above.
Each cell in the grid of your Tablet of Lore may be filled with a spell that can be cast once per rest. All spells added to your Tablet of Lore must be Meta or Primeval in genesis, and 1st League. The same spell may fill multiple cells.
Upon the completion of a rest, you may swap out one available spell with a cell. Upon leveling up, you may entirely reorganize and reassign your Tablet of Lore’s grid.
Quaternary Curator (2)
You gain access to 1 Heirloom that you fulfill the prerequisites for.
Ley Lines (3)
You gain a number of Ley Lines as shown in the Ley Lines column above, which may be moved and reorganized after each level up. A Ley Line is a horizontal or vertical highlighting of cells upon the Tablet of Lore grid. A Ley Line may be as long as you’d like in height or width, as long as the other dimension is 1 cell.
A Ley Line may overlap (usually via a perpendicular horizontal or vertical line), but no horizontal line may share the same space with another horizontal line, and no vertical line may share the same space with another vertical line.
A Ley Line atop a cell increases the League of spell you may place within that cell by 1. Multiple Ley Lines upon the same cell do not stack their effects upon that cell.
Wayfarer (4)
Your Traverse die size is increased by 1 permanently.
Your Move is increased by 1 permanently.
Tertiary Curator (5)
You now have access to 2 Heirlooms total that you fulfill the prerequisites for.
Ley Nexus (6)
A cell covered by two or more Ley Lines becomes a Nexus. Effects of Ley Lines now stack upon cells.
Expanded Catalogue (7)
Your Tablet of Lore can now possess Chronal, Corrupted, Divine, Planar, or Wyrd geneses.
Secondary Curator (8)
You now have access to 3 Heirlooms total that you fulfill the prerequisites for.
Diagonality (9)
You gain access to making diagonal Ley Lines. No diagonal line may share space with another diagonal line.
Additionally, your reach extends 1 additional space diagonally in each direction.
Rapid Recovery (10)
When you complete a breather, you may regain one expended spell of 2nd League or lower from a cell covered by a Ley Line.
Primary Curator (11)
You now have access to 4 Heirlooms total that you fulfill the prerequisites for.
Walked Legend (12)
Turn: Once per rest, regain every expended spell in one row or column of your Tablet of Lore.

rules/classes/lorewalker/lorewalker-heir.title: Lorewalker Heirlooms
rules/classes/lorewalker/lorewalker-heir.content:
LOREWALKER HEIRLOOMS
Lorewalker Heirlooms. Heirlooms do not need to be paid for.
Ancestral Heirloom
Prerequisite: Held item
While this item occupies a hand, your Evasion is increased by 1. This effect ends upon attacking or targeting a non-ally with a spell, resetting at the end of the encounter.
Annotated Heirloom
Prerequisite: Book
Turn: Once per rest, you may regain a 1st League spell on your Tablet of Lore.
Carved Heirloom
Prerequisite: Inheritor
Your Tablet of Lore is itself this Heirloom. Once per breather, you may swap the spells in two of its cells.
Cursed Heirloom
Prerequisite: Worn item
You gain -2 Defense against Necrotic and Psychic. This item is magically bound to you, and cannot be removed from your body until you die.
Heavy Heirloom
Prerequisite: Might 3
When you would be moved by an effect you did not choose, reduce the number of spaces moved by 2.
Mapped Heirloom
Prerequisite: Held item
You gain 1 flat success on all Traverse rolls.
Mended Heirloom
Prerequisite: Worn item
You gain Braced 1.
Pious Heirloom
Prerequisite: Held item
Once per rest, when you fail a roll to resist an effect, you may reroll it. While this item occupies a hand, you gain -1 Defense against Holy.
Slayer’s Heirloom
Prerequisite: Worn item
Once per encounter, you may add an additional weapon die to an attack.
Wayward Heirloom
Prerequisite: Held item
While it occupies your hand, your Move increases by 1 and you recall the exact trace of paths you’ve traveled before.

rules/classes/lorewalker/lorewalker-vari.title: Lorewalker Variant Features
rules/classes/lorewalker/lorewalker-vari.content:
LOREWALKER VARIANT FEATURES
See Lorewalker Core Class.
Ancient Weaponwork (1)
After a Train downtime activity (and during character creation), you may consider one of your weapons your Ancient Weapon.
Select one of its properties. The weapon gains the Ancient property when you wield it, which has an identical description to the chosen property.
Inheritor (1)
You gain access to 1 additional Heirloom that you fulfill the prerequisites for, on top of those from your Curator features.
Study Synergy (2)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When an ally makes a Recall or Study roll, you may add 1 die of your respective die size to their roll.
On the Move (2)
Once per Hone, when you Move, you may cast a spell that takes a turn.
Steady Focus (3)
When you are maintaining Focus, incoming damage must equal or surpass 5 to have the ability to break it.
Ward Page (3)
Turn: Cast a spell. Rather than that spell taking effect, it is charged within a piece of written information of your choice. It is cast from that written piece once it is read by someone fluent in the written language, using your stats as needed. It targets the reader’s space if possible, or itself if not.
Anecdoted Entities (4)
Turn: You inspect an entity you can perceive, adding it to your Anecdotes.

Your maximum Anecdotes are equal to your Lorewalker level. You may not repeat entity kinds, but you may replace entity kinds with others.
You gain 1 flat success to all rolls made to learn more about this entity or its kind.
You gain 1d6 to rolls resisting effects from entities of this kind.

Castquick (4)
Choose one of the following options:
Multispell
When you cast a spell of 1st League, you gain 1 Momentum.
Singlespell
When you cast a spell of 3rd or 4th League, you gain 1 Momentum.
Cross-Reference (5)
When you cast a spell from a cell orthogonally adjacent to the last cell you cast from this encounter, you gain 1 flat success on that spell’s rolls.
Olden Armorwork (5)
After a Train downtime activity (and during character creation), you may consider one of your pieces of worn armor your Olden Armor.
Select one of its properties. The armor gains the Olden property when you wear it, which has an identical description to the chosen property (considering the property’s value to be 1, regardless of its true value).
Indomitable Nexus (6)
Spells cast from a Nexus ignore their Anima.
Shared Anecdotes (6)
Prerequisite: Anecdoted Entities
Interruption (1 Momentum): When an ally makes a roll against an entity in your Anecdotes, they gain 1 flat success.
Dead Languages (7)
You can read the purpose of any written language (for example, that a book is a cookbook rather than a spellbook).
The Goal of rolls to identify linguistic information is halved.
Lent Page (7)
Turn: Touch an ally and choose an unexpended spell on your Tablet of Lore. Until your next breather, they may cast it using your stats, expending its cell.
How it Works (8)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When a spell targets you or an ally you can perceive, make a Mind-Recall roll opposed by the caster’s Mind-Craft roll. If you win, the target gains excess Periphery equal to double the spell’s League.
Twin Focus (8)
Prerequisite: Steady Focus
You may maintain Focus on 2 spells at a time. You only fail the Will Anima if you are already maintaining Focus on 2 spells when casting.
Heirloom Ward (9)
Damage you take from spells is reduced by the number of Heirlooms on your person.
Ley Walk (9)
When you cast a spell from a cell covered by a diagonal Ley Line, you may teleport up to 2 spaces before it takes effect.
Reverse Spellwork (10)
Once per breather, you may expend an unexpended spell to cast an expended spell of a lower League.
Trailblazer (10)
Allies who start their turn within 3 spaces of you gain +1 Move until the end of that turn.
Relic Surge (11)
Once per breather, when you fail a test roll, you may add a number of d8s equal to the number of Heirlooms you are meeting the prerequisite for.
Standing Wards (11)
Prerequisite: Ward Page
You may keep up to your Mind in charged pages at once. Each may trigger when read, touched, or crossed instead.
Bequest (12)
Prerequisite: Inheritor
After a rest, choose one Heirloom you have and one ally. They gain its benefit until your next rest, ignoring its prerequisite, and you keep it too.
Grand Survey (12)
You gain 1 additional Ley Line.

rules/classes/paladin/paladin-core-class.title: Paladin Core Class
rules/classes/paladin/paladin-core-class.content:
PALADIN
Faith varies from person to person. Some define it to be a warm, passive, fulfilling feeling in their chest on quiet mornings. Paladins know better, treating belief as an inherent forge. When held long enough and hard enough, when carved within the very bones of the one who feels it, knows it, that belief becomes energy. An actual force is drawn from their promises and swung like a sword.
Scholars of the phenomenon that is Conviction mutually agree it is older than religion. No culture has staked claim of it and been proven correct. The first Paladin, wielder of Conviction, was likely someone who just got back up when it was logically clear to be a pointless act. What was done with this discovery at the very beginning has since been lost, but the tradition remains. People have had the capacity to weaponize their own willpower since the first day of history, and will hold this capacity until the last.
Religions adore Paladins, along with mercenary companies and revolutionary cells. Vow systems (the practice of binding oneself to a code specific enough to actively generate Conviction) are adopted and adapted to scriptures Paladins follow. A warband may swear themselves to their comrades, a holy order may align themselves under their text’s commandments, and a grieving widow may simply bind themselves to the fact that their child will live. Conviction has never been seen judging the promise, but only whether the promise is true.
Similarly, this is likely why Paladins are very rarely the people you expect. When they aren’t the knight in gleaming armor, they could be a laborer who swore to make it home or a child who knows what they will grow up to be.
Conviction’s most remarkable (and, to its scholars, unsettling) property is that it cannot be faked. It cannot be bottled, nor can it be mimicked. Entire theocracies have experimented with this, seeing if the sincere dedication of thousands could be borrowed to substitute for a single individual’s personal motive. It cannot.

See Paladin Variant Features.
Conviction Gauge (1)
You gain a maximum Conviction equal to your Paladin level plus your Grit. When combat begins, your Conviction is at its maximum. You regain 1 Conviction at the end of each round. If an effect reduces your maximum Conviction itself, it replenishes to its original size after a rest.
Your Conviction Gauge may not be spent to act in any way out of alignment with your coremost beliefs, even while magically controlled otherwise.
Once per attack, you may spend 1 Conviction on your attack to deal 1 extra damage.
Sworn Vow (2)
Choose your Vow from the following options, gaining features from this choice immediately and your Sworn Features.

Vow of Honor
Vow of the Spell Drinker

Divine Dedication (3)
You learn 1st-League spells equal to your Grit. These spells may be Chronal, Divine, Primeval, or ones that have the word ‘smite’ in their name. Each time you level up, you may replace a chosen spell with a different spell.
Casting a Paladin spell reduces your maximum Conviction by its League, unless it’s a smite (which only spends Conviction equal to its League).
Rise Again (4)
When you Hone, up to once per rest, you may double your Conviction.
Conviction Conduit (6)
When an ally fulfills your Vow’s tenet from a trigger when you would not, you may gain the corresponding benefits as if you had accomplished it.
Test of Faith (7)
When you would be reduced to 0 Vitality, you may reduce your maximum Conviction to 0 to instead be reduced to 1 Vitality.
Dedication Optima (9)
You gain the ability to replace 1 of your chosen spells with a different spell each rest.
Additionally, your chosen spells may now be 1st or 2nd League.
Vindicated Combatant (10)
Once per attack, you may spend 1 Conviction to add 1d6 to your attack total.
Avatar of Self (12)
Your maximum Conviction now replenishes at the start of each scene.
Once per rest, when you would be reduced to 0 Vitality, you may spend 6 Conviction to instead stand with Vitality equal to your Grit.

rules/classes/paladin/paladin-variant-fe.title: Paladin Variant Features
rules/classes/paladin/paladin-variant-fe.content:
PALADIN VARIANT FEATURES
See Paladin Core Class.
Determination (1)
You may spend 1 Conviction to reroll a die on your roll resisting Hypnosis or Frightened, to no limit each roll.
Pursuit (1)
Choose one of the following options:
Loyal
Interruption (1 Momentum): When an ally within 3 spaces moves, you may spend 2 Conviction to move up to the amount moved, or your own Move, whichever is lower.
Vengeful
Interruption (2 Momentum): When an enemy within 3 spaces moves, you may spend 1 Conviction to move up to the amount moved, or your own Move, whichever is lower.
Defier (2)
When making a contested roll where you are using Might or Grit and the opponent is using both more dice and bigger dice in their roll, your success threshold is lowered by 1.
Guardian Touch (2)
Turn: Touch an entity and spend 1 Conviction to enact this effect. Focusing on continuing to touch the entity for 3 Counts triggers it, healing the target 1 Vitality. You may expend additional uses of Guardian Touch, healing the target 2 additional Vitality for each additional use expended beyond the first.
You may use Guardian Touch up to your Grit each rest.
Inspiring (3)
Prerequisite: Determination
You may spend 1 Conviction to reroll a die on an ally’s roll resisting Hypnosis or Frightened, to no limit each roll.
Judgmental (3)
Your attacks deal 1 Holy damage to enemies that attacked you or your allies before you were hostile towards them.
Leading Presence (4)
You may spend 1 Conviction to permit an ally using Interruptions to access your Momentum as a resource.
Sacred Weight (4)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When you would be moved, you may reduce the movement inflicted upon you by a number of spaces equal to your Conviction.
Bulwark Leap (5)
Interruption (2 Momentum): When an ally within your reach is hit, spend 1 Conviction and move within 1 space of them to be hit instead.
Conviction Sensitivity (5)
You regain 1 additional Conviction at the end of each round.
Martyr’s Hand (6)
Prerequisite: Guardian Touch
Your Guardian Touch triggers in 1 Count instead of 3, and may be done up to double your Grit each rest.
Necrotic Will (6)
Turn: Touch an entity and spend 1 Conviction to enact this effect. Maintaining this touch for 3 Counts triggers it, dealing 1 Necrotic to the target’s Vitality and either:

Inflicting 1 stack of Fatigue.
Locking one of their conditions of your choice (other than Fallen Over or Grabbed) into place, forcing any attempt to end it to contest your Grit-Resist, failing to end it on a failure.

You may expend additional uses of Necrotic Will, increasing the damage by 2 for each additional use expended beyond the first.
You may use Necrotic Will up to your Grit each rest.
A locked condition does not lose stacks on its own.
Reprisal (7)
You may use the Retaliate tactic by spending 2 Conviction.
Smited Edge (7)
Damage you deal from attacks that use a Smite can’t be reduced below your Grit, or below its original amount if that’s lower.
Holy Step (8)
Turn: Choose a space within 3 spaces and spend 3 Conviction to enact this effect. Focusing on this effect for 9 Counts triggers it, causing you to teleport to that location and allowing you to take a turn.
Overflow (8)
Whenever you gain Conviction while at your maximum, you may gain 1 Periphery for each Conviction that would be gained, up to your Periphery maximum.
Dedicated Defense (9)
When an enemy hits you but fails to damage your Vitality, you gain 1 Conviction.
Once per turn, when your Block reduces incoming damage to 0, you regain the Momentum spent on it.
Dedicated Offense (9)
When you reduce a hostile entity to 0 Vitality, you may gain 1 Conviction.
Heightened Optima (10)
Your maximum Conviction’s value is increased by 5.
Unbroken Stand (10)
When your Periphery is broken, you gain Conviction equal to your Grit.
Blinking Steps (11)
Prerequisite: Holy Step
Whenever your Holy Step is triggered, you may automatically reenact the effect by spending its previous Conviction cost plus 1.
Unending Conviction (11)
You may use Rise Again twice per rest instead of once.
Obliterating Strike (12)
When a die explodes, you may spend 2 Conviction to cause it to grant a second die to roll as well, to no limit.
Paladin Maxima (12)
Prerequisite: Guardian Touch, Leading Presence, and Smited Edge
When you start your turn at maximum Conviction, you gain the following features until the end of your turn:

Your spells reduce your maximum Conviction by 1 less, to a minimum of 1.
Your Guardian Touch does not cost Conviction.
Your Conviction Gauge’s once-per-attack spend may be used up to 5 times per attack.

rules/classes/paladin/vow-of-honor.title: Vow of Honor
rules/classes/paladin/vow-of-honor.content:
VOW OF HONOR
A Paladin Vow.
Tenets of Honor
Set the Match.
You gain 2 Conviction when you clearly declare your goal for this combat. This may be done once per encounter. You may not spend Conviction in a manner which counters this goal.
Match and Above.
You gain 2 Conviction when an enemy team gains more participants, or when you grant an enemy an advantage against you without aiding yourself (up to GM discretion; for example, giving them a better weapon or discarding your own).
Above the Belt.
You gain 1 Conviction when you attack an enemy in your reach that is not Fallen Over while there is an enemy that is.
You may not spend Conviction attacking enemies who are Fallen Over while there is an enemy who is not.
Sworn Features
Shield of the Civil (2)
You cannot be surprised by attacks from enemies you knew were there. When a non-participant in combat is attacked when you were an available target, the non-participant is granted Strong Cover.
Interruption (1 Momentum): When an entity within your reach attacks an entity not hostile towards the attacker, you may attack the attacker.
Combat’s Call (5)
When you hit an enemy with an attack, you may make them your Called Combatant. They remain your Called Combatant until they are no longer conscious, until you are no longer conscious, or until the scene ends. You may not possess more than one Called Combatant at a time. When you are making an attack roll against your Called Combatant, you may spend any amount of Conviction to add that much Conviction spent to your damage total.
Motivesense (8)
Turn: You may spend 4 Conviction to become capable of sensing the underlying drive that will fuel one’s decisions in the coming moments. All entities within 4 spaces are assigned one of the following terms depending on which is closest to their active plan, until the end of the encounter:

Appeal: This Called Combatant gains 1 stack of Frightened of you.
Deception: This Called Combatant’s Move is reduced by 1, and they cannot benefit from Weak Cover or Strong Cover from you.
Escape: This Called Combatant’s Move is reduced to yours if it was higher, and Momentum spent to increase their Evasion against attacks fails to increase their Evasion at all, though secondary effects still work.
Loyalty: This Called Combatant’s subtractive Defenses are halved against damage sources from you and your allies.

You are aware of this assignment, and you gain the listed feature in relation to them when they are your Called Combatant.
No Rest for the Moral (11)
You may possess up to 2 Called Combatants (both of which you may select in a single use of Combat’s Call), and your Combat’s Call’s die size increases to a d8.
Interruption (1 Momentum): When you would be knocked unconscious or reduced to 0 Vitality while a non-participant’s life is at stake, you may instead spend 1 Conviction to remain conscious, or to remain alive at 1 Vitality, and gain 1 stack of Fatigue. At the end of this encounter, your Fatigue rises to 3 stacks if it was lower. Each use of this increases its Momentum cost by 1, to no limit.

rules/classes/paladin/vow-of-the-spell-d.title: Vow of the Spell Drinker
rules/classes/paladin/vow-of-the-spell-d.content:
VOW OF THE SPELL DRINKER
A Paladin Vow.
Tenets of The Spell Drinker
Be The Sword.
You gain 1 Conviction when you hit an enemy while they are casting a spell.
Be The Shield.
You gain 1 Conviction when a magical effect targeting an ally you can see is stopped or ends.
Be The Spell.
You gain 1 Conviction upon casting a 2nd-League spell (or higher).
Modified Class Features
Divine Dedication (3)
Your chosen spells may also be Meta or Planar.
Sworn Features
Expeditious Command (2)
Turn: You may target however many entities you can see, spending 2 Conviction per entity. These entities are invigorated with a sudden surge of force, granting them each 1 Momentum. Your Periphery takes 1 damage per entity invigorated.
Absorb Magic (5)
You possess an Antimage Aura that extends in all the spaces of Reach 3.
Interruption (2 Momentum): When a spell is triggered within your Antimage Aura, you may spend (3 + the spell’s League) in Conviction to siphon the spell. If the spell’s League is equal to or smaller than a third of your level, it does not take place, and is considered sufficiently siphoned.
If the spell is sufficiently siphoned, you gain triple the spell’s League in Periphery (not limited by your maximum), and you regain Conviction equal to the spell’s League.
Aura of Disruption (8)
All enemies ending their turn within your Antimage Aura must make a Grit-Recall roll against a third of your Paladin level. If they fail, they lose Focus on all spells they were maintaining. These spells are considered siphoned.
Greedy Gullet (11)
Whenever you siphon a spell, you may store its League as your stolen magic value. You may only have one value stored at a time, and may only dispel this value from its storage by fueling yourself with it.
Turn: You fuel yourself, allowing you access to any of the following features:

You may consider your Speed to be your stolen magic value higher when you Move or Sprint.
You may deal your stolen magic value in Anomalous damage to an enemy that casts a spell.
You may add your stolen magic value to an opposed roll in which you are the defender.

rules/classes/psychedel/psychedel-core-c.title: Psychedel Core Class
rules/classes/psychedel/psychedel-core-c.content:
PSYCHEDEL
(Flavor needed)

Deliriant (1)
Your Dissonance is a pool representing the tightness of your grip on reality. It starts at 0. Upon achieving a rest, your Dissonance is halved.

You know a number of 1st-League Cerebral and Wyrd spells equal to your Psychedel level. You may reselect these upon each level-up. Starting at Psychedel level 8, the spells you know may be 1st or 2nd League.
When you cast a spell this way, you expend Dissonance equal to its League, and reduce your Lapse Threshold by that same amount. You cannot cast a spell if you have insufficient Dissonance, or if your Lapse Threshold is lower than the spell’s League.
When an effect would raise your Dissonance above your Lapse Threshold, your Dissonance is instead set to your Lapse Threshold minus 1, and you Lapse.

Vice of Choice (2)

Vice of the Draught

A Figment appears to be whatever can inhabit that corresponding quantity of space, and can be discovered to be a disturbance in reality with a Mind-Find roll against your current Dissonance. It is dealt 1 card each round. It instantly vanishes when reduced to 0 Vitality, or when you rest.
When your Figment vanishes, you may choose to gain 2 Dissonance.
The following is the attack a Figment possesses, using your stats:























NameAttributeSkillDieTypeReachPropertiesFigmentMindd4d4Chemical/Psychic2Reinforced 1
Figments roll a d4 in place of a Skill die.
Daydream (4)
Turn: You may spend 1 Dissonance to make up to a singular cubic space not inhabited by any entities instantly and permanently vanish from existence.
Turn: You may spend 1 Dissonance to manifest up to a singular cubic space of any form of material. You must maintain focus on the object by continuing to touch it. It vanishes in its entirety upon no longer being touched.
Contact High (6)
You gain -(the number of entities within a number of spaces equal to your current Dissonance) Defense against Psychic.
All entities within a number of spaces equal to your current Dissonance gain +1 Defense against Psychic.
Turn: An entity you are touching must make a Grit-Resist roll against your Mind-Break or see reality as you perceive it. If you succeed, they take an amount of Psychic damage equal to the difference of successes between the rolls.
Mind Palace (7)
Turn: If your Dissonance is above half your Lapse Threshold, you may reduce your Lapse Threshold by 2 to temporarily override a number of unoccupied equally-vertical spaces equal to your Dissonance, changing them into any of the following, with more up to GM discretion. At the end of the encounter, the effects undo, transforming the spaces back to what they were upon enacting this.

Everything within the space vanishes, becoming fully empty air.
Everything within the space is filled with a solid material totaling a ton of weight.
Everything within the space is filled with a slime-like ooze.

Lucid (9)
When you Lapse, you may add or subtract your Grit from the d100 roll.
Shared Delusion (10)
Your Figments may be any size up to your current Dissonance, and have Vitality equal to their size.
Ego Death (12)
Once per rest, when you would Lapse, you may instead set your Dissonance to 0 and restore your Lapse Threshold to its full value.

rules/classes/psychedel/psychedel-varian.title: Psychedel Variant Features
rules/classes/psychedel/psychedel-varian.content:
PSYCHEDEL VARIANT FEATURES
See Psychedel Core Class.
Imaginary Friend (1)
An entity of your choice (up to GM discretion) takes a form beside you. This is your Imaginary Friend. Your Imaginary Friend is not real, does not inhabit space, is in no way tangible, and is of no volition to follow your commands or obey you in any form. If it ever is to make a roll, it uses your stats.
Your Imaginary Friend cannot leave your sensory perception, or it vanishes until it is re-‘perceived’.
Turn: You send your sensory capabilities into theirs, being able to use your senses through them as if they were real and there. During this time, you lose all sensory capacity.
Trip Sit (1)
When you take a breather with an ally, you may increase or decrease your Dissonance by 1.
Bad Trip (2)
When your Vitality is damaged, you gain 1 Dissonance.
Manifested Friend (2)
Turn, or during your turn for 2 Momentum: You may temporarily allow your Imaginary Friend to enter existence as an entity sharing your stats and resource pools (including Periphery, Vitality, Evasion, etc.). It, however, possesses its own unique size and has /2 Defense against all damage. You maintain Focus by making a Grit-Resist roll against damage taken to your real body, losing it upon a failure.
You may dismiss the manifestation of your Imaginary Friend, making them no longer real.
When you make an attack, you may attack from your Imaginary Friend while it is Manifested.
Pareidolia (3)
Your Figment’s attack gains Staggering.
Second Opinion (3)
Prerequisite: Imaginary Friend
While your senses are within your Imaginary Friend, you gain 1 flat success on Find rolls.
Migraine (4)
Your Headache’s Range becomes your Grit plus your current Dissonance.
Paranoia (4)
Interruption (1 Momentum): When you are attacked, you may swap places with one of your Figments within Grit spaces. The attack targets the Figment instead.
Comedown (5)
When you complete a breather, you may lose any amount of Dissonance, restoring half that amount to your Lapse Threshold.
Phantom Limb (5)
Prerequisite: Manifested Friend
While Manifested, your Imaginary Friend may Retrieve and Grab.
Echo Chamber (6)
When your Figment vanishes, all entities within 1 space of it (orthogonally or diagonally) take 1 Psychic.
Thousand-Yard Stare (6)
While your Dissonance is above half your Lapse Threshold, you gain 1 flat success on rolls resisting Frightened and Hypnosis.
Folie à Deux (7)
Prerequisite: Imaginary Friend
Choose one ally. They can perceive your Imaginary Friend, and may use its senses as you do.
Night Terror (7)
When your Headache damages a target’s Vitality, they gain 1 stack of Frightened of you.
Hive of Figments (8)
Your Figment spawns 2 Figments instead of 1, for the same cost.
Spiral (8)
When you Lapse, you gain 3 Momentum.
Ego Shield (9)
When your Periphery is broken, you gain Dissonance equal to your Grit.
Hollow Reality (9)
Your Daydream may affect up to a number of cubic spaces equal to your Grit at once.
Doppelgänger (10)
Prerequisite: Manifested Friend
While Manifested, your Imaginary Friend is dealt 1 card each round and takes its own turns.
Waking Nightmare (10)
Your Mind Palace gains the following option:

Everything within the space is filled with lightless darkness.

High Tolerance (11)
Your Lapse Threshold becomes your Psychedel level plus double your Grit.
Mass Hallucination (11)
Your Contact High’s Turn may target every entity within Grit spaces of you, rather than one you are touching.
Dream Logic (12)
Once per rest, you may cast a spell without expending Dissonance or reducing your Lapse Threshold.
Imaginary Army (12)
Prerequisite: Doppelgänger
You may have a second Imaginary Friend, which may also be Manifested.

rules/classes/psychedel/vice-of-the-drau.title: Vice of the Draught
rules/classes/psychedel/vice-of-the-drau.content:
VICE OF THE DRAUGHT
A Psychedel Vice.
(Flavor needed)
Vice Features
Dosage (2)
You begin with 4 Doses. You can carry up to double your Psychedel level in Doses. Doses cost 6 Leptom, have Scarcity 3, and are acquired through provisioning.
During your turn, you may spend 1 Momentum to consume a Dose on your person to increase or decrease your Dissonance by an amount up to 3, taking 1 Chemical damage (which may not be reduced) to your Vitality.
Formulary (5)
When you provision for a Dose, you may select one of the following options to opt for its Scarcity and to gain its effect, along with the previous:

Heighten (Scarcity 4): Your Lapse Threshold decreases by 1. Your areas of effect are increased in size by half in each dimension.
Lessen (Scarcity 2): You take an additional 2 Anomalous damage when you take this Dose. In areas of effect you impose, you may select up to half the targeted entities to be unaffected by it.

Tolerance (8)
Your Doses no longer deal Chemical damage.
Cocktail (11)
You may consume two Doses at once, gaining both of their Formulary effects.

rules/conditions/bleeding.title: Bleeding
rules/conditions/bleeding.content:
Bleeding
Bleeding stacks.

At the end of each round, you lose 1 Vitality.
While your Vitality is below your stacks, you are unconscious.
When you would gain Vitality, your stacks of Bleeding are removed instead.

rules/conditions/blinded.title: Blinded
rules/conditions/blinded.content:
Blinded

You cannot perceive by sight.
Your attack rolls are decreased by 4 whenever hitting the target would use sight at all. Avoiding this through hearing requires a feature.

rules/conditions/burning.title: Burning
rules/conditions/burning.content:
Burning

At the end of each round, you take 2 Heat to your Vitality.
Spending a turn, or 2 Momentum, ends this condition.

rules/conditions/deafened.title: Deafened
rules/conditions/deafened.content:
Deafened

You cannot perceive by sound.
You automatically fail all rolls requiring hearing, such as hearing someone speak to you, even against a Goal of 0.

rules/conditions/fallen-over.title: Fallen Over
rules/conditions/fallen-over.content:
Fallen Over

Your Evasion is halved against melee attacks, and increased by 2 against ranged attacks.
Your melee reach is halved in spaces, rounded up.
Your Move is halved.
You can stand when you move, spending all of your Move to do so. This ends the condition.
Only entities on a surface can be fallen over.

rules/conditions/fatigue.title: Fatigue
rules/conditions/fatigue.content:
Fatigue
Fatigue stacks.

All incoming damage is increased by 1 per stack.
Your Move is decreased by 1 space per stack, to a minimum of 1. While your Move is 1 or lower, you cannot Sprint.
Your Test rolls lose 1 success per stack.
You are never considered to beat a Goal by more than 5 minus your stacks.
If your stacks equal or exceed your Grit + 2, you die.
Whenever you gain Vitality, you lose 1 stack, regardless of how much Vitality you gain.
If you would gain Vitality but cannot due to being at your maximum, your stacks are halved, rounded down.

rules/conditions/frightened.title: Frightened
rules/conditions/frightened.content:
Frightened
Frightened stacks, and its stacks are tracked separately for each source of fear.

Test rolls targeting or resisting the source are made with 1 less die per stack, to a minimum of 1 die. Attack rolls against the source take -1 to the attack total per stack.
You cannot willingly move closer to the source.
You cannot Hone.
If your stacks exceed your Mind, you must spend each of your turns moving away from where you believe the source to be, and you may only spend Momentum to move away from it.
At the end of each round in which you cannot perceive the source, you lose 1 stack. If the source is destroyed, all stacks end.

rules/conditions/grabbed.title: Grabbed
rules/conditions/grabbed.content:
Grabbed

You cannot move away from your grabber. When your grabber moves, they may drag you with them at half their Move.
Your Evasion is halved.
You may Break Free on your turn. An object holding you, such as cuffs or glue, has a Goal to beat instead of an opposed roll.
The grab ends if your grabber lets go, is moved away from you, or cannot act.

rules/conditions/hypnosis.title: Hypnosis
rules/conditions/hypnosis.content:
Hypnosis
When you are hypnotized without clarification as to which aspect of hypnosis you are affected by, the context surrounding the effect is the aspect. Otherwise, you are inflicted with the respective aspects of hypnosis.

Charmed: You cannot willingly target the source with any attacks or harmful effects. You cannot negatively impact the source in any way as you understand it, including harming their allies.
Compelled: You change sides, becoming an ally to the source. Your turn is dictated by the source. If it does not have an ability to dictate this for you, you instead behave normally, as if the source is still your ally (for example, maybe only trying to talk your former allies down rather than striking them). You are, however, violently defensive on behalf of the source, keeping the source protected by whatever means are sensible to you.
Transfixed: You cannot willingly look away or turn your attention away from the source. You may not spend Momentum.

rules/conditions/invisible.title: Invisible
rules/conditions/invisible.content:
Invisible

You cannot be perceived by sight.
You are hidden, as with the Hide action.
You gain 2 flat successes on rolls made to avoid being perceived.

rules/conditions/staggered.title: Staggered
rules/conditions/staggered.content:
Staggered
Staggered stacks.

Your Evasion is reduced by 1 per stack, to a minimum of 0.
Test rolls made to resist effects lose 1 success per stack.
If you reach 6 stacks, you become fallen over.
At the end of each round, you lose 1 stack.

rules/conditions/surprised.title: Surprised
rules/conditions/surprised.content:
Surprised
When you are surprised, you were unprepared for an event as it transpires before you.

You cannot spend Momentum.
You cannot enact a Periphery Cleanup.
Surprised ends once the first round of combat has passed.

An entity considered surprised by an attack suffers these effects against that attack only, without gaining the condition.

rules/conditions/unconscious.title: Unconscious
rules/conditions/unconscious.content:
Unconscious

When you are unconscious, you become fallen over.
You cannot take turns, act, or think, and you cannot gain or spend Momentum.
Natural unconsciousness (such as sleep) can be ended by loud noises, being pushed, or taking damage. More imposing means of unconsciousness, such as conditions or spells, require their own unique ends to be met to conclude the effect.

rules/gear/armor-properties/bearing.title: Bearing
rules/gear/armor-properties/bearing.content:
Bearing
Compare the value following Bearing to your Might. For each point it exceeds your Might, your Move is decreased by 1 space, and your die size is decreased by 1 step on all rolls using Might, Speed, or Grit, and on the Skill die of all attack rolls (not the weapon die).

rules/gear/armor-properties/braced.title: Braced
rules/gear/armor-properties/braced.content:
Braced
When you Block, reduce all incoming damage (besides Psychic or Anomalous) by the value following Braced.

rules/gear/armor-properties/loud.title: Loud
rules/gear/armor-properties/loud.content:
Loud
Your die size is decreased by a number of steps equal to the value following Loud on Dodge rolls.

rules/gear/armor-properties/uncaught.title: Uncaught
rules/gear/armor-properties/uncaught.content:
Uncaught
While your Periphery is at or above its maximum, your Evasion is increased by the value following Uncaught.

rules/gear/armor-properties/underlayer.title: Underlayer
rules/gear/armor-properties/underlayer.content:
Underlayer
This armor may be worn beneath Rivet or Ferrum armor. While worn this way, its Defense applies, and it increases the properties of the outermost armor by the respective modifiers in parentheses.

rules/gear/armor-properties/unmoving.title: Unmoving
rules/gear/armor-properties/unmoving.content:
Unmoving
Rolls you make to resist being pushed or moved gain 2 additional dice.

rules/gear/armor.title: Armor
rules/gear/armor.content:
Armor

The era each armor originates from is yet to be decided.























































NameDefensePropertiesLeptomScarcityCachette, Patch CloakUncaught 2151Cachette, Wambeis-2 BluntUnderlayer (Bearing +1)151Rivet, Laminan-4 SliceBraced 1, Loud 13603Rivet, Scute-3 Puncture / SliceBearing 3, Loud 11202Ferrum, Aegis-4 Blunt / Puncture / SliceBearing 4, Loud 112004Ferrum, Fortress-4 Blunt / Puncture / SliceBearing 6, Braced 2, Loud 3, Unmoving30005
Cachette
Cachette armors are for the quick or intellectual. They are layered soft goods, being cheap to make and replace. They are near-universally the first armor anybody wields. The word ‘Cachette’ refers to the term smugglers would use for a hollow beneath a floorboard, and the naming conventions have stuck around as mortalkind coalesced a proper universal language.
Patch Cloaks
A patch cloak is a weighted, many-paneled garment cut so that the hem, shoulders, and trailing edges never sufficiently settle on a moving target. These panels are dyed in mismatched, broken patterning and hung on staggered fitted extensions, so that the wearer presents a silhouette that is too inaccurate to sufficiently read in combat. Oftentimes, this makes them appear approximately half a step away from where they’re actually standing, which is meant to buy enough time for victory to be taken.
Patch cloaks are an open and blatant attempt at nonmagically replicating illusions, and it’s not lost on the consumers or producers. It’s oftentimes advertised AS an illusory imitation. However, patch cloaks fail to survive the same scrutiny of magic. Thankfully for patch cloak wielders, though, in the first exchange, an opponent who does not know the shape of their enemy is at so massive a disadvantage that it’s kept them in circulation for combatants since their initial productions.
Wambeis
Canvas and quilted linen are stuffed densely with cheap fibers, stitched in tight channels that keep the fillings in place. A wambeis is bulky, hot, and admittedly grating to wear without buying high quality enhancements, but they are astonishingly resilient to blunt force.
As the most common piece of armor among common mortals, a wambeis is used by those more like warriors as a piece beneath the real equipment. Rivets and Ferrums are meant for the outer shells, while final blows are just not enough when a wambeis lies under the outer layers.
Rivet
Rivet armors are built from the fastening of small pieces into a flexible surface. They are for those incapable of dodging impacts and those incapable of bearing intense weights. When force arrives on a Rivet, its goal is to spread and deflect the force. It works against almost anything, but as a general term, excels at nothing in particular.
Laminan
Laminan are full body suits of rings, each link closed individually and worked into a mesh that hangs oftentimes from the jaw to the ankle, if not from a sprouting pot-shaped helm and draping beneath the user entirely. Laminan thus possesses no particular seam to be pierced, which is highly effective. The main problem is that the labor required is so enormous that Laminan’s price is almost entirely derived from the amount of time it takes to bind.
Laminan, due to their price, are placed upon soldiers that are fielded and expected to return home, or at least return for multiple combats. Laminan’s inability to dramatically fail makes it constantly repaired, and Laminan that are in use are typically of a minimum age equal to the country utilizing it.
Armories inherit, resize, and pass Laminan along. Due to Laminan being ridiculously loud, experienced soldiers can oftentimes identify the exact number of soldiers wielding them in a march.
Scutes
Scutes are overlapping plates of bone, horn, boiled hide, and occasionally metals, depending on the region and wealth. They are laced onto a backing so that each rides over the edge of the others, and the finished piece covers the torso and shoulders in a shell, resembling a scrap carapace of sorts.
Scutes protect less of the body than many other armors of equal value, but they protect the parts they are upon far better, and the plates are individually replaceable easily enough that they are financially maintainable, even while being far away from an armory. Frontier hunters, caravan guards, and other travelers make good use of scutes.
The tradeoff is typically considered to be in the concentrated weight upon the chest and shoulders, punishing the underbuilt badly enough to be only worth it if you are of martial physique. If you cannot wear a scute and you attempt to, you are more likely than not to be worse than dead weight.
Ferrum
Ferrum is the articulated plate, large shaped sections of metal fitted to a body. It is by far the most expensive, requiring fitting processes of weeks. They can’t even be meaningfully resold to any extent, meaning that a ferrum suit has become a universal icon for someone who expected to be repeatedly attacked by competent foes, as well as someone who expects to repeatedly win.
Aegis
The aegis is the classic suit, being a giant mass of steel equipment hinged and strapped over an arming layer. An aegis is fitted rather than being sized, and the plates follow the wearer’s actual proportions closely enough that, when taken from someone else, it is worse than nothing. Aegises are visual shorthand for the armored warrior across functionally any culture. Oftentimes they are enameled by orders or houses in order to publicize that a successful warrior is allied strongly with them. The traditional path of gaining one is done through ascending the weight categories of lighter armors.
Fortress
A fortress armor is an aegis taken past typical points of reason. The plates are thicker, doubled at every angle a weapon could possibly arrive from, and mounted upon an internal frame that raises the wearer’s apparent height by nearly half a foot. Fortress-wearers exist for siege lines, break points, the front rank of formations, and occupying doorways or thresholds. The armor is near-deafening in motion (especially on a physically capable enough user), impossible to be even equipped solo, and they possess such intense power that it requires vehicles or small armies of laborers to carry individual sets. However, despite all of these downsides, it is the most effective piece of equipment at keeping someone alive.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/ambush.title: Ambush
rules/gear/weapon-properties/ambush.content:
Ambush
If the target is surprised, or considered surprised by your attack, roll this weapon’s die twice and add both results to the damage.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/ammo.title: Ammo
rules/gear/weapon-properties/ammo.content:
Ammo
After attacking with this weapon, it must be fully reloaded before it can attack again. Fully reloading it takes a number of Retrieve actions equal to the value following Ammo.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/bimanual.title: Bimanual
rules/gear/weapon-properties/bimanual.content:
Bimanual
If this weapon has the Bimanual property outside of a parenthesis, then it requires being held in both hands to be used.
If this weapon has the Bimanual property inside of a parenthesis, then the property it is bound to is only active while the weapon is held in both hands.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/enhanced-cr.title: Enhanced Crit
rules/gear/weapon-properties/enhanced-cr.content:
Enhanced Crit
Whenever a die explodes on an attack with this weapon, roll 2 dice of that size instead of 1.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/flurry.title: Flurry
rules/gear/weapon-properties/flurry.content:
Flurry
Interruption (2 Momentum): Upon hitting with this weapon and resolving its damage, you may make another attack with it. That attack’s total is decreased by 1.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/gutting.title: Gutting
rules/gear/weapon-properties/gutting.content:
Gutting
When you damage a target’s Vitality with this weapon, deal an additional die of damage of the size following Gutting.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/parry.title: Parry
rules/gear/weapon-properties/parry.content:
Parry
When you Sidestep while wielding this weapon, your Evasion is increased by an additional amount equal to the value following Parry.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/perforate.title: Perforate
rules/gear/weapon-properties/perforate.content:
Perforate
Nonmagical means of mitigating this weapon’s damage, such as Defense from armor, Blocking, or Braced, only mitigate half as much.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/plant.title: Plant
rules/gear/weapon-properties/plant.content:
Plant
Turn: Slam this weapon into the ground and hold it there, gaining the effects in parentheses following Plant. It stays planted until you remove it, as a turn or at the cost of 1 Momentum.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/reinforced.title: Reinforced
rules/gear/weapon-properties/reinforced.content:
Reinforced
Your attack total with this weapon is increased by the value following Reinforced.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/staggering.title: Staggering
rules/gear/weapon-properties/staggering.content:
Staggering
When you hit with this weapon, the target gains 1 stack of Staggered.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/telescopic.title: Telescopic
rules/gear/weapon-properties/telescopic.content:
Telescopic
Extending or retracting this weapon costs no Momentum, and may be done once per round. This weapon only takes a hand while it is extended.

rules/gear/weapon-properties/wind-up.title: Wind-Up
rules/gear/weapon-properties/wind-up.content:
Wind-Up
Instead of attacking with this weapon immediately, choose a target or space within reach. The attack is made a number of Counts later equal to the value following the Wind-Up property.
This property cannot trigger an attack if another property of the weapon would trigger an attack on the same Count.

rules/gear/weapons.title: Weapons
rules/gear/weapons.content:
Weapons

The era each armor originates from is yet to be decided.
