Knives
Discra Knives
A handle connected to a crescent-shaped blade, meant for disabling and able to be thrown by talented users.
Hymn Knives
A dagger hidden in a wrist-mounted strap, able to thrust the blade forward when the hand bends up, allowing for rapid strikes and unoccupied hands.
Incise Knives
Incise Knives are specifically constructed with the purpose of multi-tooling and simplicity. They are sharp, one-sided, maneuverable blades you can effortlessly use to cut food, vegetation, or attackers with. Almost all homes possess at least one thanks to their constant usefulness and low cost.
Spade Knives
A handle connecting to an almost rose-like tunnel of overlapping blades. When stabbed into terrain, lifting it out will pull whatever you stabbed. Using centrifugal force, a swing will deject whatever was lodged inside of the hollow cylinder, slinging it out of the sharp top-end. This allows for quick injurious attacks.
Swords
Basket Swords
Basket swords are durable, classic, one-handed weapons that are meant to emphasize versatile balance alongside an above-average defense. The most recognizable aspect of this is the hilt, often referred to as the ‘basket,’ being a rounded and shielded dome over your hand to protect from grazes or glancing impacts.
Typically, basket swords are used by more agile guardsmen, or poorly trained fighters with access to decent equipment. They are very friendly to minor mistakes, unlike almost any other weapon, and this allows them to shine in less talented engagements.
Crown Swords
Crown swords are elite, balanced, well-made two-handed weapons meant for classically trained warriors. They are mass-producible, but are able to be used by genuinely talented swordsmen with amazing effects.
Yatakh Swords
Brutish and giant, Yatakh swords are hefty and mighty blades, often almost 5 times longer than their two-handed grip. While usable by the highly talented, their true use comes from exploiting brutish amounts of force in attacks.
Bows
Spire Bows

Description needed

Pneumas
Pneumas are made to obtain and then tighten immensely to create pressure, before releasing it in one sudden and massively damaging projectile.
Log Pneumas
A sculpted mass from a tree, with strings made from fibers in the wood, made to load long sharpened things to blast.
Shields
Ballist Shields

Description needed

Facade Shields
A facade shield is meant to be held out straight in front of you while you wait to make use of it for extremely easy deflections.
Guillotine Shields

Description needed

rules/glossary.title: Glossary
rules/glossary.content:
Glossary
Every definition below is taken from where the term is defined. Follow the link for the full rule.





















































































































































































































































































TermDefinitionAttack ModificationAttack Modifications are unique to Tactics, and are applications on any attack you are making. You may not enact multiple Attack Modifications at once.Attack RollAttack rolls compare a single total against a target’s Evasion, and are used for attacks.AttributeEpitaph is composed of 5 Attributes. Your Attributes are defined by a flat number.AnimaAnima are the conditions under which a spell can be drawn upon.BlockDouble your Defense against an incoming instance of damage.BleedingA condition. Bleeding stacks.BlindedA condition. You cannot perceive by sight.BreatherA breather is around 30 minutes of light, stationary activity or sleep.BrokenIf Periphery reaches 0, it becomes broken (or breaks, both terms are used).BurningA condition. At the end of each round, you take 2 Heat to your Vitality.CountA round is a single, full loop of combat, made up of individual steps called Counts. Counts descend from 10 to 1 and repeat each round.CoverAn obstruction between an attacker and their target grants the target cover against that attack.DeafenedA condition. You cannot perceive by sound.DeathIn Epitaph, a character dies when they reach 0 Vitality.DefenseYour Defense is a list of conditional modifiers applied to each instance of incoming damage, before it is allocated to Vitality and Periphery.Die SizeThe ladder is d4 -> d6 -> d8 -> d10 -> d12.DowntimeDowntime is an extended period, ranging anywhere from days to years.EncounterSegments within scenes that account for individual elements, like a fight or a conversation. They are best individualized by smooth transitions to different tones or styles of interaction with the setting. For example, a conversation between two drunkards devolving into a tavern brawl are two different encounters within the same scene of the tavern.EnactingTimed effects are triggered (have their effect take place) asynchronously from when they’re enacted (caused or used by the wielder of the timed effect).EvasionAn entity’s Evasion is equal to 6 at a baseline, and is increased by means of features, equipment, and environmental factors.Excess PeripheryPeriphery may be raised above its maximum, up to double its maximum, but only by effects that explicitly grant excess.ExplosionAlongside the effects of rolling a die’s maximum face, roll one more die of the same size. This is called an explosion.Fallen OverA condition. Only entities on a surface can be fallen over.FatigueA condition. Fatigue stacks.Flat SuccessA flat success is added to your success count without rolling a die, and cannot explode.FocusSome spells require Focus to maintain their effects or to finish being cast.FrightenedA condition. Frightened stacks, and its stacks are tracked separately for each source of fear.GenesisEvery spell has a Genesis, the nature and source of its magic.GoalGoals are a number of successes required from a roll to have a chosen result occur.GrabbedA condition. You cannot move away from your grabber.HandsYou have 2 hands, and each holds one object.HoneRegain 2 Momentum, and recharge features relying on it, such as sprinting.HypnosisA condition. When you are hypnotized without clarification as to which aspect of hypnosis you are affected by, the context surrounding the effect is the aspect.InterruptionAn effect marked Interruption (# Momentum) is something you do at that cost in response to the trigger that follows it.InvisibleA condition. You cannot be perceived by sight.LeagueSpells are graded in Leagues from 1st to 4th, dictating their potency.LeptomThe currency is Leptom. 1 day’s pay is about 3 Leptom.MomentumMomentum is a resource spent on effects outside of the typical turn economy, such as reacting, intercepting, and making smaller actions without losing your turn.MoveYour Move is a series of values (each with an assigned series of tags) that determines the means by which you travel.Opposed RollWhen a character acts directly against another, this is an opposed roll, where both parties make their relevant rolls, and the higher success count wins.OriginAn origin is the mechanical impact of who a character was before the campaign began.PeripheryPeriphery is the surface-level avoidance and ability to keep damage from truly making harmful contact.Periphery CleanupWhen damage would break your Periphery while you aren’t surprised, you may enact a Periphery Cleanup, which lowers the amount of damage that would’ve been dealt to your Vitality by your maximum Periphery.Progression PointsEach time you gain a level, you gain progression points equal to your new level.RangeRanged weapons have a Range, the farthest number of spaces they can attack.ReachReach 1 covers every space adjacent to you, diagonals included. Each additional point of Reach extends one space further in every direction.RestA rest is at least 8 hours of heavy sleep.Rest TimerYou must finish a rest within 14 + (Grit x 2) hours of finishing your previous one.RoundA round is a single, full loop of combat, made up of individual steps called Counts.ScarcityEvery good has a price in Leptom and a Scarcity. Scarcity is whether you can find a good, and price is whether you can afford it.SceneSegments of narrative that the GM dictates. They are best individualized by the backdrop/environment itself shifting, or a metaphorical hard cut between moments. For example, a conversation between two drunkards devolving into a tavern brawl are the same scene, but the cut to the character waking up after being knocked out cold is the beginning of a new scene.ShiftShift is exclusively a Momentum expense on your turn. It moves you 1 space, and cannot be spent standing up.SidestepIncrease your Evasion by 2 against an incoming attack.SizeEntities possess a volume and three dimensions.SkillSkills range from d4 to d12, which is functionally the spectrum of foreign to master.SpaceDistance is measured in spaces, with 1 space being 5 feet.SprintMove up to five times your Move.StaggeredA condition. Staggered stacks.Success4 is the success threshold. Rolling this or anything higher on a die qualifies it as a success.Success ThresholdThis changes only what counts as a success, which is 4 by default.SurprisedWhen you are surprised, you were unprepared for an event as it transpires before you.TacticTactics are alternative attacks and Interruptions that can be gained, and further augmented, by other abilities.Test RollTest rolls count successes against a Goal, and are used for most uncertain tasks.TurnAn effect marked Turn is such an action, and using it takes your turn.UnconsciousA condition. You cannot take turns, act, or think, and you cannot gain or spend Momentum.VectorVectors define a spell’s area and targets.VitalityYour Vitality is the meat, your capacity for actual harm.

rules/origins/index.title: Origins

rules/origins/priest.title: Priest
rules/origins/priest.content:
Priest
Your time and servitude are dedicated to a temple or religious tie, often to a god or a particular pantheon of them. You act as an intermediary between the holy and mortals, performing rites and prayers.

+1 Speak or Study Die Size
+1 Recall Die Size
20 Leptom

Divine Ingrainment
You gain a 1st League Divine or Primeval spell that you may cast up to twice per rest. You may change your chosen spell after the Recuperate downtime activity.

rules/origins/soldier.title: Soldier
rules/origins/soldier.content:
Soldier
You served in an organized fighting force of some kind, whether that be a mercenary cell, city watch, or bandit posse. While that particular era is behind you, it’s failed to fully leave you. You have instilled within yourself the protocol for combat.

+1 Break or Aim Die Size
+1 Recall Die Size
35 Leptom

Take Initiative
Once per rest, when a new round begins, you may be dealt 1 additional card.

rules/origins/storyteller.title: Storyteller
rules/origins/storyteller.content:
Storyteller
You spent, at the very least, your youth following the shifting and complex cultural tides of the world, pursuing participants in the odder spots external to the public eye. This led to a mixed and full life lived in (relative) safety, and an intense hunger for attention.

+1 Dodge or Handle Die Size
+1 Speak Die Size
20 Leptom

Way With Words
When you spend at least a minute communicating with someone not hostile, you may make a Speak roll opposed by their Charm-Instinct roll. If you succeed, you can hypnotize them (Transfixed) until the communication ends, or until something startling occurs (screaming for help, an attack beginning, etc.).

rules/origins/student.title: Student
rules/origins/student.content:
Student
You are still in your youth. With your story not yet having fully distilled itself against the prologue, you are malleable and able to make the most of your lack of competence.

+1 Craft or Recall Die Size
+1 Study Die Size
10 Leptom

High Potential
When you are going through character creation, your Skill points are increased by 2. Additionally, instead of being lost if unspent, they are banked as progression points.

rules/roll-examples.title: Roll Examples
rules/roll-examples.content:
The table below is not exhaustive, and purely demonstrative of the reasoning a GM generally should follow.

Aim (Precision / Throwing / Shooting)

Might: Pinning someone to a wall with a spear or piercing armor with an arrow
Speed: Landing a headshot on a moving target or hitting targets rapidly
Mind: Accounting for wind and distance or bouncing a shot off a surface
Grit: Slow-and-steady aim while bleeding out or holding aim while being rushed
Charm: Calling for help to make a target turn for a headshot or making a trick shot especially flashy


Break (Dismantling / Destroying Something / Lockpicking / Shoving / Opening / Intimidation)

Might: Shoving someone aside or ripping something apart
Speed: Lockpicking or knocking something loose in the middle of a sprint
Mind: Striking in the perfect spot or taking apart a machine
Grit: Wearing restraints down or striking for hours on end
Charm: Intimidating someone into backing down or sabotaging a defense


Craft (Making / Building / Tool-Usage / Improvisations)

Might: Bending stock to shape by hand or seating a joint that won’t seat
Speed: Field-repairing something as it fails or assembling something as fast as possible
Mind: Building to a specification or improvising a tool out of scrap
Grit: A design that takes days or increasing something’s quality as you decline in health
Charm: Making a creation especially appealing or appealing a design for a particular taste


Dodge (Evading / Hiding / Balance / Avoiding Harm / Stealth / Blending In)

Might: Deflecting a shove or pushing back into balance
Speed: Slipping beneath cover or balancing in micro-adjustments
Mind: Predicting an incoming danger or choosing the safest path in traps
Grit: Continuing to evade after being struck down multiple times or staying hidden in an uncomfortable space
Charm: Blending into a crowd or pulling attention away


Find (Perceiving something through senses/logic/manual investigation)

Might: Sensing hollow spots in a dense object or prying through secure containers
Speed: Spotting movement from the corner of your eye or catching a hidden movement
Mind: Piecing together clues or logically deducing a series of events
Grit: Searching a forest for hours or methodically analyzing a room
Charm: Picking up on body language or realizing why a witness won’t talk


Handle (Motor Control of Objects / Steering / Grappling / Carrying / Lifting / Dragging)

Might: Moving something heavy or intense grip strength
Speed: Steering through tight obstacles or juggling
Mind: Operating complex machinery or delicately guiding instruments
Grit: Holding a grapple for extended time or maintaining steady control through turbulence
Charm: Coordinating others in a movement or helping a dance partner


Instinct (Gut reaction / timing / primal/natural knowledge/connection)

Might: Connecting to nature or giving in to adrenaline
Speed: Snatching something before it hits the ground or reflexive timing
Mind: Intentional timing or recognizing danger instantly
Grit: Fighting fear or staying alert while dying
Charm: Recognizing conversational tension or making intense art


Recall (Using previous experiences / following protocol)

Might: Using techniques or following a combat drill
Speed: Planning a fast getaway or remembering the right fact in the right moment
Mind: Encyclopedic knowledge or recalling a very particular moment long ago
Grit: Following procedures when in severe pain or making a calculation while exhausted
Charm: Following foreign cultural customs or remembering an old friend’s preferences


Resist (Enduring/Withstanding/Ignoring/Fighting Through Exhaustion)

Might: Shrugging off intense strain or pushing back against physical attacks
Speed: Shaking off disorientation to continue a fine movement or adjusting to being magically slowed
Mind: Ignoring psychological controls or rationally contesting eldritch forces
Grit: Pure determination or continuing long after others have stopped
Charm: Holding morale or ignoring intense insults


Speak (Language / Persuasion / Commanding / Insulting / Deception / Communication / Storytelling / Dancing / Music)

Might: Speaking louder than others or silencing a crowd
Speed: Quick wit or talking your way out of trouble
Mind: Learning a language or explaining complex ideas clearly
Grit: Speaking coherently or rallying others through a crisis
Charm: Audibly performing or getting what you need in a conversation


Study (Gaining new information, whether from databases or insight upon someone)

Might: Testing materials or excessively practicing simpler skills
Speed: Picking up a technique immediately or adapting throughout practice
Mind: Reading documents or understanding complex theories
Grit: Studying through long hours or mastering highly complex skills
Charm: Asking insightful questions or drawing out hidden knowledge


Traverse (Navigating Environments/Terrains/Walls/Traps)

Might: Climbing rough surfaces or forcing through hazards
Speed: Sprinting across rooftops or unstable parkour
Mind: Observing safe paths or optimally navigating environments
Grit: Crossing harsh terrain or moving when you physically shouldn’t
Charm: Keeping a mount calm or making conversation during journeys


Treat (Enhance something’s wellbeing)

Might: Fixing dislocated joints or holding broken things together
Speed: Fixing something while it is failing or being the first to aid in an emergency
Mind: Extensively technical procedures or diagnosing conditions
Grit: Maintaining equipment over time or long-term care
Charm: Comforting or inspiring someone in distress

rules/species/elf.title: Elf
rules/species/elf.content:
Elf

Appearance, Lore, Society, and Names needed

Traits

Personality needed

Lifespan
Grove Elves live around 250 years. Wyv Elves effectively do not age after reaching maturity, so long as the dragon they are in symbiosis with remains within them.
Size
Elves are approximately 6’1” to 6’6”, and effectively never become heavier than 160 lbs.
Attribute Bonus
+1 Mind
Learned Past
+1 Die Size to any of the following Skills 4 times: Craft, Find, Instinct, Recall, or Study.
Memories
You have 5 Memories, each a single sentence describing an event that occurred within your long lifespan. Each Memory can be drawn upon once per rest, in either of the following ways:

When a Memory reminds you of the situation, you may add 2 flat successes to a Test roll, or 2 to an attack roll’s total, after its outcome is known.
You may ask any question about the context of a Memory. It is answered with at most a single sentence of its own.

During the Recuperate downtime activity, you may reword any Memory to describe the same event. Upon leveling up, you may replace any Memory with another, including recently experienced ones or another from before the campaign.
Ancestries
Wyv Elf

Description of Wyv Elves needed.

Nigh-Ageless
You gain 2 flat successes on rolls defending against Chronal spells.
Draconic Memory
The dragon within you holds 1 additional Memory, written with the GM, which cannot be changed. When drawn upon to add to a roll, it grants 3 instead of 2. Until it is drawn upon, you gain /2 Defense against one damage type, chosen when the Memory is written.
Grove Elf

Description of Grove Elves needed.

Earthbound
You gain a flat success on all Find and Speak rolls while within dense environments of nature.
Extraordinary Hearing
You can discover the location of any source of sound within 2 spaces of you. When you make a Find roll based on your sense of hearing, you may decrease the Success Threshold by 1.
While you are blinded, you are immune to its decrease to your attack rolls, as long as you can hear at all.
Listening Ground
Once per rest, while within dense environments of nature, you may gain a temporary Memory, written by the GM, about something that happened there. It fades once it is drawn upon, or once you gain a different temporary Memory. When drawn upon to add to a roll, it grants 3 instead of 2.

rules/species/mongrel.title: Mongrel
rules/species/mongrel.content:
Mongrel
Appearance, lore, society, and name examples needed.
Traits
Personalities needed.
Lifespan
Mongrels live around 90 years.
Size
Mongrels can be anywhere from 4 to 7 feet tall, and anywhere from 15 to 30 inches wide.
Attribute Bonus
+1 to any Attribute.
Discordant Anatomy
Once per rest, when you would gain a stack of Fatigue or Staggered, you may ignore it.
Graft
You may replace a part of your body with that of a corpse, requiring the Recuperate downtime activity and a Mind-Treat or Grit-Treat roll against a Goal of 3. On a success, you gain one of the following benefits:

+1 die size to a Skill the donor’s anatomy plainly served
-1 Defense against a damage type the donor’s anatomy granted them defenses against
+1 Reach or +1 Move

You may have up to 1 graft, 2 once you reach level 3, 3 once you reach level 6, and 4 once you reach level 9. A graft beyond this limit replaces the benefit of one of your previous grafts. Each of your grafts must grant a different benefit.
If you fail in your attempt to graft, you gain 2 stacks of Fatigue, and may not attempt to graft until they’re gone.
Nonsensical Silhouette
You cannot be identified as a member or hybrid of any collection of species. Rolls made to determine your species, recall your kin, or predict your anatomy’s behavior automatically fail. You may add 1 die to Might-Break or Charm-Break rolls made to intimidate someone with your body’s capability.
Ancestries
Mongrels have no ancestries. They cannot reproduce.

rules/species/index.title: Species

rules/species/syrinx.title: Syrinx
rules/species/syrinx.content:
Syrinx
Appearance
Syrinx are lean, feathered, and oftentimes have faint undercurrents of magic perceptible to the sensitive. Other than this, their featherings cover the avian spectrum, with eyes often embodying weathered colorations (silver, black, teal, etc.).
Name Examples
Syrinxian names are often combinations of 1 to 2 syllables using whistle-based phonetics, such as Whisskyr, Cirrus, and Lihi.

Lore and societies are needed.

Traits
Personality
Syrinx are infamously abrupt, poetic, and communal. Many refuse to walk when able to fly otherwise, as ground contact is deeply ingrained with a connotation of loss and mourning. Oddly enough, this culture is not actively used in most modern society, but instead comes from an ancient culture that has progressed intensely since then. Despite their capabilities often rooting from traditional tools and talents, Syrinx value change and speed above almost all else. The only thing able to compete with that is their inclination toward groups and societies, as any Syrinx embedded in diverse cultures will almost always find an even prouder evaluation of the importance of community.
Lifespan
Syrinx live around 60 years.
Size
Syrinx are 4’11” to 5’9”, and cap at around 70 lbs.
Attribute Bonus
+1 Speed or +1 Charm
Avianoid
You gain /4 Falling Defense. You breathe normally in thin air and at high elevation, and can maneuver without effects from wind.
Feathered Motes
You have 4 Feathered Motes, and you regain them each rest.

You may spend a Mote when you deal damage to a grounded entity while you are at least 6 spaces away from them, making a Speed-Aim roll opposed by their Might-Resist roll. If you win, they gain 1 stack of Staggered.
You may spend a Mote to add 2 dice to a roll contesting an effect impeding your ability to move.
You may spend a Mote to redraw one of your dealt cards.
Interruption (1 Momentum): When you would move from a freefall, you may spend 1 Mote to instead hover in place for 1 full round.

Windbound
You gain (Speed + 2) Flight. The wings granting this capacity force you to wear armor that is approximately 1.5x more expensive.
Ancestries
Belowbound
A Syrinxian lineage severed from the air, genetically engulfed in the forces of stone. As such, they have wings of dry, muddied, flaking greyish brown, mismatched with their other feathering. These wings are wildly heavy, durable, and maneuverable.
Mantled Wings
You lose the Windbound feature. However, you gain -1 Blunt / Puncture / Slice Defense.
When you Block incoming Blunt, Puncture, or Slice damage down to 0, you may regain the Momentum spent on the Block. You must Hone before being able to do so again.
Tremor Strike
You may make a Tremor Strike, swinging your stone wing into anything nearby. This attack uses the Sweep tactic.
Tremor Strike | Might | Handle | d8 | Blunt | Reach 1 | Reinforced 1

rules/spells/1st-league/acid-splash.title: Acid Splash
rules/spells/1st-league/acid-splash.content:
Acid Splash
You fire a globule of volatile bile, summoned from a planar cauldron. The acid spews forth, melting the target.
This spell triggers 3 Counts after it is enacted. The target makes a Speed-Dodge roll, taking 1d4 {2d4, 3d4, 4d4} Chemical damage, plus that much again for every 1 below the Goal of 2 {3, 4, 5}.

rules/spells/1st-league/afterimage.title: Afterimage
rules/spells/1st-league/afterimage.content:
Afterimage
You coerce an illusory duplicate of yourself into forming, upholding your former placement in time and space.
When you leave a space, an illusion of you remains in it for 10 {20, 30, 40} Counts.

The afterimage looks and sounds exactly as you did when you left the space. It does not move or act.
Entities that did not see you leave believes you are still in the space.
Any entity may Search to see through the afterimage, against a Goal of 2 {3, 4, 5}.
An attack against the afterimage passes through it and misses, revealing it as an illusion to the attacker only.
You may only have one afterimage at a time. Casting this spell again ends the previous one.

rules/spells/1st-league/annum-bolt.title: Annum Bolt
rules/spells/1st-league/annum-bolt.content:
Annum Bolt
You dip your fingers into the nigh-infinite rivers of time, scooping out a sufficient divergence to point and fire.
Make an attack roll using Mind and Instinct. Its die is a d4 {d8, 2d6, 2d10}, and it deals Anomalous damage.

rules/spells/1st-league/blade-ward.title: Blade Ward
rules/spells/1st-league/blade-ward.content:
Blade Ward
You intone an oath older than weapons, and translucent sigils drift around your target. For a moment, your external form mimics the settlement of steel and resilience of iron.
For 10 {20, 30, 40} Counts, your target gains -2 {-4, -6, -8} Blunt / Slice / Puncture Defense.

rules/spells/1st-league/brain-fog.title: Brain Fog
rules/spells/1st-league/brain-fog.content:
Brain Fog
You flood the neurons of one’s mind with a violent surge of redundancy and confusion, destroying their ability to think straight.
When an entity within range enacts an effect that requires Focus, including beginning an Extended casting, you may cloud their train of thought.
The target makes a Mind-Resist roll against a Goal of 2 {3, 4, 5}. If they fail, they lose track of what they were doing, and the effect fails. Any resources they spent to enact it remain spent.

rules/spells/1st-league/cloak-of-mana.title: Cloak of Mana
rules/spells/1st-league/cloak-of-mana.content:
Cloak of Mana
You pull upon the arcane ambience surrounding you, forming a loose draped surface that pulls taut on any spells that dare reach through.
You gain 3 {6, 12, 24} excess Periphery. You gain 1 {2, 4, 7} flat successes on rolls defending yourself against spells. This lasts as long as you maintain Focus upon it.

rules/spells/1st-league/delta-fog.title: Delta Fog
rules/spells/1st-league/delta-fog.content:
Delta Fog
You call upon the ancient spirituals rituals of the river, calling upon their hallucinatory pollutions to destroy the differentiation of real and unreal.
A low fog fills the space. While within the fog, illusions cannot be differentiated from reality.

rules/spells/1st-league/doorlink.title: Doorlink
rules/spells/1st-league/doorlink.content:
Doorlink
You assess the multidimensional coordination of two thresholds and scramble them.
Any two doorways with a two-dimensional size of 4 {9, 16, 25} spaces or lower are connected for the remainder of the encounter, without Focus. Anyone who moves through one moves out of the other (from either side of it).

rules/spells/1st-league/echoed-impact.title: Echoed Impact
rules/spells/1st-league/echoed-impact.content:
Echoed Impact
Upon an exchange of force, you incur it a second time. You draw it back like a band and allow it to slam back once again.
When an entity deals Blunt or Anomalous damage, one of the entities it damaged takes that damage again as Anomalous, up to 3 {6, 12, 24}.

rules/spells/1st-league/eldritch-blast.title: Eldritch Blast
rules/spells/1st-league/eldritch-blast.content:
Eldritch Blast
You unleash a rupture of foreign will, woven from primordial logic, manifesting as an uncoiling spiral of fractured light and shadow that lashes out towards your target.
The target takes 1d4 {2d4, 3d4, 4d4} Anomalous damage. This has 1 {2, 3, 4} target(s).

rules/spells/1st-league/element-flash.title: Element Flash
rules/spells/1st-league/element-flash.content:
Element Flash
You strike an unseen surface between the elements, erupting forward a shockwave of primordial sporks.
Roll 1 {2, 3, 4} d10(s) to determine the damage type(s) and corresponding effect(s), rerolling duplicate types.

1–2: Cold. Reduce the target’s Move by 1 space for 10 {20, 30, 40} Counts.
3–4: Chemical. The target must allocate at least half of the damage to their Vitality.
5–6: Sonic. The target gains 1 stack of Staggered.
7–8: Electric. Targets lose successes equal to this spell’s League on their roll against it.
9–10: Heat. Deal an additional 1 {2, 4, 8} damage.

All targets must make a Grit-Resist roll against a Goal of 2 {3, 4, 5}. If they fail, they take 1d10 of each rolled damage type, and suffer the rolled effect(s).
If they succeed, they still take half the damage, but negate the effect.

rules/spells/1st-league/fortunate-contac.title: Fortunate Contact
rules/spells/1st-league/fortunate-contac.content:
Fortunate Contact
You invoke the blessing of Kismet, temporarily granting them a spree of elusiveness and beginner’s luck.
When either you or an entity moves while they are within your reach, you may touch them, granting them 1 {3, 6, 9} excess Periphery. Additionally, the target gains the following feature, which it may use up to 1 {2, 3, 4} times in this scene.
Interruption (0 Momentum): Completely reroll a roll before you are confirmed to have failed or succeeded.

rules/spells/1st-league/gift-of-certaint.title: Gift of Certainty
rules/spells/1st-league/gift-of-certaint.content:
Gift of Certainty
You form a mold of a statement, slipping it into the folds of one’s brain and leaving it to marinate for as long as their body fails to notice.
The target makes a Mind-Resist roll opposed by your Mind-Speak or Charm-Speak roll. If they fail, they are filled with a simple, verifiable piece of information. They undoubtedly believe it for 1 {8, 24, 168} hours.
If they receive evidence directly contradicting the fact they were given, they snap out of the effect, and become aware that this piece of information was inflicted upon them rather than believed of their own volition.

rules/spells/1st-league/hasten.title: Hasten
rules/spells/1st-league/hasten.content:
Hasten
You grab a hold of the cords, and accelerate a select few forward along it.
Each target is dealt 1 additional card next round.

rules/spells/1st-league/herald-home.title: Herald Home
rules/spells/1st-league/herald-home.content:
Herald Home
You bestow your attention upon something small and incomparable to yourself, granting it a purpose. Within an instant and without hesitance, it readies itself to fulfill the purpose you have given it.
Choose a pitiful entity local to this environment’s wildlife. You gain means of commanding and controlling the entity through a specific aspect of hypnosis for the following 24 {168, 8760, ∞} hours. Select a location you have been to, describe an entity it could comprehend, and give it a written means of communication to bring to that entity. It will attempt, by any and all means, to successfully bring that communication to that entity, using its own intellect and means of mobility.

rules/spells/1st-league/holy-smite.title: Holy Smite
rules/spells/1st-league/holy-smite.content:
Holy Smite
Your strike emits an intensely glowing and wildly potent beam of energy focused into the target, landing with enough force to potentially burst through the opposite side.
Upon hitting a target, your attack deals an additional 1d4 {2d4, 4d4, 8d4} Holy damage.

rules/spells/1st-league/invert-harm.title: Invert Harm
rules/spells/1st-league/invert-harm.content:
Invert Harm
An injury is turned inside out, becoming a brief arcane pool of fortune and survival, protecting them as long as it may.
When an entity takes damage to their Vitality, you may grant the target 2 {4, 8, 16} excess Periphery plus the Vitality damage taken, up to 3 {6, 12, 21} total.

rules/spells/1st-league/paelu's-gravity-.title: Paelu's Gravity Well
rules/spells/1st-league/paelu's-gravity-.content:
Paelu’s Gravity Well
You grab the corners of reality like a foldable fabric, and drape it within one consecrated spot.
Move within the field is halved. An entity that ends its turn inside loses 1 Momentum.

rules/spells/1st-league/phantom-weight.title: Phantom Weight
rules/spells/1st-league/phantom-weight.content:
Phantom Weight
You trick a mind into believing that something it has a hold of has become vastly heavy, too much to handle.
The target makes a Mind-Resist roll opposed by your Mind-Speak or Charm-Speak roll. If you win, choose one object they are holding or wearing. They become convinced it is far heavier than it is.
For 10 {20, 30, 40} Counts, they suffer Bearing‘s penalties as if the object possessed a Bearing value of 4 {6, 8, 10}.
If they stop holding or wearing the object, this spell ends.

rules/spells/1st-league/pocket-pocket.title: Pocket Pocket
rules/spells/1st-league/pocket-pocket.content:
Pocket Pocket
As if it were only sleight of hand, you flip something out view of existence itself.
An object in your hand vanishes into a safe extradimensional space fitted exactly to it.
Turn: You may bring back or re-vanish the object.
This effect lasts as long as you maintain Focus on it.

rules/spells/1st-league/pressure-smite.title: Pressure Smite
rules/spells/1st-league/pressure-smite.content:
Pressure Smite
Your strike folds reality while blasting into it, causing it to burst outward towards in a select chain.
When you make an attack, its reach is extended by 2 {4, 6, 8}, and it may target up to 3 {4, 6, 9} entities. Each target after the first must be the nearest untargeted entity to the previous target, allies included, so it may not skip entities. Upon hitting a target, they must make a Might-Traverse roll against a Goal of 3 {4, 6, 9}. If they fail, they become fallen over.

rules/spells/1st-league/read-mind.title: Read Mind
rules/spells/1st-league/read-mind.content:
Read Mind
A thread of your own attention worms its way into another’s, surfacing their mental interface to be overheard as if it were a mumbling to the self.
The target makes a Mind-Resist roll opposed by your Mind-Study or Charm-Study roll, plus 1 {2, 3, 4} flat success(es).
If they succeed, they feel something is off, and become aware that a spell is affecting their mind.
If you succeed, you can empathetically bind to their mind, reading their biggest concern, motivations, reasonings, and big terms or phrases common within their thoughts.

rules/spells/1st-league/recall.title: Recall
rules/spells/1st-league/recall.content:
Recall
An object of yours become the subject of your mind’s eye, before you push it away to focus on other tasks. And when this object is to become yours again, it will, no matter the space between you.
Mark an object you are holding. At any time, at no cost, you may call it back to your hand from up to 6 {12, 60, 600} spaces away. This does {does not, does not, does not} require focus.

rules/spells/1st-league/ringing.title: Ringing
rules/spells/1st-league/ringing.content:
Ringing
You send a backlash of intense energies to the brainstem or equivalent neurological foundation of one who inflicts you with pain.
When you take damage, you deal 1d4 {2d4, 4d4, 8d4} Psychic damage back to the source of the damage (if you can perceive them). All of this damage must be allocated to Vitality.

rules/spells/1st-league/swap.title: Swap
rules/spells/1st-league/swap.content:
Swap
You highlight volumes of space, and swiftly switch them before unsettling the underlying forces.
Select two entities to instantly switch places, taking the other’s position and inheriting their respective environmental conditions. If an entity is unwilling to be swapped, they may make a Grit-Resist roll opposed by your Grit-Break roll.

rules/spells/1st-league/time-to-think.title: Time to Think
rules/spells/1st-league/time-to-think.content:
Time to Think
You take a moment to inhale, and time does not pass. You think, think some more, and ensure your thoughts are clear. As you exhale, you are several steps ahead of the others.
Make a Search and Hone action. For the next 9 {20, 40, 80} Counts, your Evasion is increased by 1. This does not stack with itself.

rules/spells/1st-league/tripwire.title: Tripwire
rules/spells/1st-league/tripwire.content:
Tripwire
You find a space to be crossed, and stitch within it a pattern that holds no purpose but to break. The finished line is mindless and invisible, with one function it exists to serve.
Select a threshold for the surface to cover, limited in diameter to 10 {25, 100, 400} spaces. Select entities to not trigger the spell. If an entity passes this threshold while you are within a mile of it, you wake up if you weren’t already awake, and become aware of something having breached the spell’s chosen threshold.
Once cast, this spell does not require Focus.

rules/spells/1st-league/unbowed.title: Unbowed
rules/spells/1st-league/unbowed.content:
Unbowed
Yielding is not something to take lightly. You ensure this is known.
Up to 1 {2, 4, 7} target(s) end Staggered and Fallen Over on themselves. Those targets cannot gain Staggered from any effect for the following 10 {20, 30, 40} Counts, unless it deals damage to their Vitality.

rules/spells/1st-league/wet-clay.title: Wet Clay
rules/spells/1st-league/wet-clay.content:
Wet Clay
You hide a method of communication in the incommunicable properties of an object. In this case, the dryness.
Speak a message into clay and carve a mark into it. The first entity to wet the clay hears the message once, in your voice. The clay holds the message for 1 {7, 30, ∞} days.

rules/spells/2nd-league/binding-barriers.title: Binding Barriers
rules/spells/2nd-league/binding-barriers.content:
Binding Barriers
You generate a thin film of raw time, manifested and faintly sparking.
Nothing can pass through or damage the barrier. At the start of each of your turns, you may move the barrier up to 5 spaces, as long as it stays within 10 spaces of you.

rules/spells/2nd-league/entropic-reversa.title: Entropic Reversal
rules/spells/2nd-league/entropic-reversa.content:
Entropic Reversal
A strike that would harm you is surgically pulled outside the events of time, while you safely remain in the present.
When an ally takes damage, up to 6 {12, 24} of it is negated, and they gain excess Periphery equal to half the negated amount.

rules/spells/2nd-league/eroding-reverb.title: Eroding Reverb
rules/spells/2nd-league/eroding-reverb.content:
Eroding Reverb
You do your best to grasp the cords and shake them as violently as you can to protect yourself and your allies.
You and every ally within the area gain a Reverb until the end of the encounter.

Interruption (1 Momentum): Spend your Reverb to increase your Evasion by 2 {3, 4} against an incoming attack.

rules/spells/2nd-league/erycrinth's-tran.title: Erycrinth's Transfusion
rules/spells/2nd-league/erycrinth's-tran.content:
Erycrinth’s Transfusion
You facilitate the life force between two bodies, no matter the crudeness or brutality.
Your first target is the donor, who must be either a corpse or willing. Your second target is the recipient. The donor takes 1 Necrotic damage, which must be allocated to Vitality. For every point of damage the donor took from this, the recipient gains 1 Vitality. You may repeat this effect up to once per round, until either:

The donor is no longer willing.
The donor is a corpse, and has taken an amount of Necrotic damage equal to its volume (causing it to crumple and turn to dust).
The donor, if alive at first, dies.
A minute passes.

When this spell ends, the donor gains 1 stack of Fatigue.

rules/spells/2nd-league/glasswork-counte.title: Glasswork Counter
rules/spells/2nd-league/glasswork-counte.content:
Glasswork Counter
(Flavor needed)
When a spell is cast, you may make a Mind-Craft roll opposed by the caster’s Mind-Recall roll to decrease the League of the spell by 2 {3, 4}. If it is decreased to 0 or below, it automatically fails to be cast, still expending all of the caster’s respective resources.

rules/spells/2nd-league/hourglass-bucket.title: Hourglass Bucket
rules/spells/2nd-league/hourglass-bucket.content:
Hourglass Bucket
(Flavor needed)
You make a Mind-Handle roll opposed by the target’s Grit-Instinct roll, in which you gain 0 {1, 3} flat successes. If you succeed, you steal 1 card from their next round’s deal, gaining it in your own deal instead. An entity becomes immune to Hourglass Bucket for the remainder of the scene after being targeted with it, success or fail.

rules/spells/2nd-league/slow-bolt.title: Slow Bolt
rules/spells/2nd-league/slow-bolt.content:
Slow Bolt
You attempt to pin an enemy at a place on the cord. Even if for a moment, it violently slows the target upon contact.
Make an attack roll using Mind and Instinct. Its die is a d4 {d8, 2d6}, and it deals Anomalous damage. If none of its damage is reduced by Defense or Block, the target loses 2 {3, 4} Momentum.

rules/spells/2nd-league/slumber.title: Slumber
rules/spells/2nd-league/slumber.content:
Slumber
You generate a surge of restful chemicals, forcing everyone to sleep regardless of preference.
Every entity within the area (except yourself, if you wish), including allies, makes a Grit-Resist roll against a Goal of 3 {4, 5}. Entities that do not sleep are unaffected.
Those who fail fall asleep, becoming unconscious for up to 1 {10, 60} minutes. This is natural unconsciousness, so it ends early from loud noises, being pushed, or taking damage. Shaking or pushing a sleeper awake takes a turn.

rules/spells/2nd-league/vita-stabilizer.title: Vita Stabilizer
rules/spells/2nd-league/vita-stabilizer.content:
Vita Stabilizer
In an effort to keep yourself and any others physically afloat, you rapidly redistribute all quantities of life.
You and any willing entities you choose within the area add your current Vitality together and split it evenly, without exceeding anyone’s maximum. You distribute any remainder.

rules/spells/3rd-league/infinite-gravity.title: Infinite Gravity
rules/spells/3rd-league/infinite-gravity.content:
Infinite Gravity
An inevitable drag rapidly shunts everything inward in a bubble around you.
Every other entity within the area is pulled to the nearest space adjacent to you, or as close as it can get. Each makes a Grit-Resist roll against a Goal of 3 {4}. On a failure, it takes 3d10 {6d10} Anomalous damage. On a success, it takes half.

rules/spells/3rd-league/repetitio-bomb.title: Repetitio Bomb
rules/spells/3rd-league/repetitio-bomb.content:
Repetitio Bomb
A pulsating energy bursts again and again, suffusing those of synergy with speed.
Any ally starting their turn within the field gains 1 Momentum.

rules/spells/4th-league/paradox-singular.title: Paradox Singularity
rules/spells/4th-league/paradox-singular.content:
Paradox Singularity
Until the end of the scene, or until you dismiss it at no cost, roll a d8 at the start of each round. The result takes place for that round.

All entities lose all Momentum.
All entities regain all lost Momentum.
Every entity in the combat takes 4d6 Anomalous damage.
Every entity in the combat decreases their Evasion by 2.
Every entity in the combat increases their Evasion by 2.
You are dealt an additional card.

Roll twice, rerolling 8s.

Tactics are gained through features, or purchased with progression points at a price that depends on the tactic.
